<thought>The NMR data show a para‑disubstituted benzene (4 aromatic protons, 4 distinct aromatic carbon signals) and a cyclohexyl group attached via a benzylic CH (44 ppm) to the ring (10 H multiplet at 1.35 ppm from five CH₂ groups, 1 H at 2.63 ppm from the benzylic CH). No carbonyl or hetero‑atom signals are present, so the second para substituent must be a non‑protonated, non‑hetero atom group such as a halogen. The simplest structure matching these data is para‑bromo‑(or chloro‑)cyclohexylbenzene, i.e., a benzene ring bearing a cyclohexyl group at one para position and a bromine (or chlorine) at the opposite para position. Both give the same NMR pattern; the exact halogen can be distinguished by mass spectrometry. I will retrieve the mass spectrum to see the molecular ion and confirm the halogen.</thought>
